A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same K-Viscuit benchmark and human-VLM construction framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original VLM evaluations, a Korean/non-Korean human study, language comparisons, generative QA results, and retrieval-augmentation experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds visual-dependency, answer-order sensitivity, and Type 1 grounding experiments.

M1.justification: The concept selection, image selection, GPT-4-Turbo question generation, and human verification framework remains unchanged. v3 renames Type 2 and clarifies filtering practices without establishing a revised construction procedure. The new prompting and input manipulations are diagnostic evaluation conditions.

E1.justification: The 657-question benchmark, ten cultural categories, languages, human populations, and existing comparison datasets remain the same. v3 adds an evaluation scenario with meaningful images replaced by Gaussian noise, changing the available visual information without expanding cultural or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: The model rosters in the retained benchmark, language, cross-dataset, and retrieval comparisons are unchanged. v3 newly evaluates GPT-4o-mini with and without Type 1 context in Appendix A.3 and Table 8, a limited expansion confined to that analysis.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation procedures with same-size Gaussian-noise image controls, circular evaluation across four option rotations with an all-variation consistency requirement, and Type 1 QA pairs supplied before Type 2 questions. These introduce distinct controls and scoring conditions; the existing main evaluation settings and results are retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark diagnostics: visual dependence in Section 4.2/Figure 7, option-order robustness in Appendix A.1/Figure 9, and the effect of Type 1 grounding in Appendix A.3/Table 8. Appendix A.2 also extends the existing CVQA comparison with an audit of shortcut answers and implausible distractors. Earlier analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly reports standard deviations of 2.69 for Korean participants and 5.95 for non-Korean participants, alongside the unchanged means and boxplots. The participant counts remain unchanged, and no increase in experimental runs or new significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Substantial new results document overall accuracy drops of 10.4–23.1 percentage points with noise images and relative drops of 16.9–30.4% under circular evaluation. Table 8 reports GPT-4o-mini Type 2 accuracy of 74.31% without and 81.30% with Type 1 context. These are new experimental comparisons, not improvements over v2 under identical conditions. Existing Tables 2–7 retain their results; Table 5 only increases decimal precision.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs. The added circular-evaluation criterion is an empirical testing protocol, without accompanying mathematical derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same framework, benchmark, and proprietary-versus-open-model claims. The conclusion modestly narrows its description of the performance gap from understanding Korean culture to identifying Korean cultural concepts and explicitly mentions limitations of open-ended evaluation.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation of what benchmark scores measure. It interprets noise-image results as evidence of visual dependence and Type 1 assistance as supporting cultural reasoning. Appendix A.1 and the Limitations section newly explain possible positional bias and warn that option shuffling may be insufficient, adding an important qualification to MCQA score reliability.

D1.justification: v3 adds the concept-to-IDS mapping in Appendix B.1/Table 9, clarifies exclusion of abstract images and recognition-only Type 2 questions, newly discloses option shuffling, and identifies the authors as manually selecting oracle documents. These clarify existing practices rather than establish changed construction settings. Existing prompts, model implementation details, and dataset access remain available.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bhatia et al. on multicultural VLM evaluation, Liu et al.'s MMBench for circular evaluation, and Zheng et al. and Pezeshkpour and Hruschka on option-order sensitivity. The expanded CVQA discussion adds specific criticisms of shortcuts and distractor consistency, sharpening the positioning of human-VLM construction while preserving the broader related-work narrative.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites question-type and verification explanations, renames Type 2 as Cultural Knowledge Application, merges Results and Analyses, reorders the human and language discussions, and renames Discussion as Future Directions. It reorganizes the appendices and updates author information and acknowledgements, while retaining most prose and the overall narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adds diagnostic Figures 7 and 9 and appendix Tables 8 and 9. The dataset-example and framework figures exchange order, several retained displays move, and captions gain clarification, including the framework stages and retrieval scope. These are targeted additions and layout adjustments within the existing visual design.

improvement.justification: The new image-ablation and option-order tests make benchmark validity and score sensitivity easier to assess, while clarified construction details improve transparency. These provide a useful, limited gain over v2's existing evaluation evidence. The grounding analysis adds support, although its statement of gains across categories overstates Table 8: Beverage and Religion show ties.
